name: Brazil
summary_text: Brazil combines some of the world's strongest legal protections for transgender people with a high level of real-world violence — the classic gap between law and practice. Courts allow name and gender-marker changes without surgery, the Supreme Court has criminalised transphobia (making it punishable like racism), courts fine businesses that discriminate, and official guidance affirms trans people's right to use bathrooms matching their identity. For visitors, big-city queer life is vibrant and highly visible — São Paulo hosts the world's largest Pride parade — and the law is unambiguously on a trans traveller's side. The practical risks are concentrated in nightlife and app-based meetings: a majority of physical violence against LGBTQIA+ people in São Paulo happens at night, and robbery schemes luring gay men via dating apps have been fatal. Exercise particular caution after dark, with nightlife and app meetings, and in peripheral areas. Violence against local trans people (Brazil records the world's highest absolute toll) is heavily concentrated in poor and marginalised communities, not tourist areas.

sources.claim_summary: Wikipedia overview of LGBTQ rights in Brazil: covers the 2018 Supreme Court rulings on gender identity (self-declaration of gender marker; name/gender change without surgery), non-binary recognition, healthcare, conversion-therapy ban, anti-LGBT violence, and social conditions. Same-sex marriage recognised since 2013.

sources.title: Brazil | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): marriage equality since 2013 (with congressional repeal efforts underway); 2019 Supreme Court ruling prohibits discrimination and hate crimes based on SOGI; trans people can change gender markers by self-determination. Brazil continues to have one of the highest rates of violence against sexual and gender minorities, particularly trans people; 3,000+ openly LGBTQ candidates ran in the 2024 municipal elections.

Brazilian law firm guide (April 2026) for expats: same-sex marriage, spousal visa equality, adoption, and name/gender-marker changes are available; notes Brazil has no comprehensive federal anti-discrimination statute, with protections built from court rulings.

sources.title: Violências e golpes contra pessoas LGBTQIA+ na noite de São Paulo
sources.claim_summary: Agência Pública (May 2024, in Portuguese): investigation into violence against LGBTQIA+ people in São Paulo nightlife - 57% of physical-violence incidents against LGBTQIA+ people in the capital occurred at night; victims report insecurity in bars and clubs.

AP (Oct 2024): 'Death threats assail Brazil's trailblazing trans candidates as they campaign' — nearly 1,000 transgender politicians run in municipal elections across every state amid threats and intimidation, as the number of trans officeholders has tripled since the last cycle.

sources.title: Trans barrada em boate por usar roupa feminina será indenizada
sources.claim_summary: ConJur (May 2025, in Portuguese): São Paulo Court of Justice upheld a moral-damages award against a nightclub that barred a trans woman for wearing feminine clothing ('bustiê e minissaia'); the court held trans people have the right to treatment conforming to their social identity and raised the compensation to R$10,000.

sources.title: The inclusion of Trans People in the law to prevent violence against women in Brazil - Latinoamérica 21
sources.claim_summary: Latinoamérica21 (2022): Brazil's Superior Court of Justice unanimously held that the Maria da Penha Law (domestic-violence protection) applies to transgender women, based on gender rather than biological sex - after lower courts had twice denied protection to a trans woman attacked by her father.

sources.title: CPI da Violência Contra Pessoas Trans e Travestis - Portal da Câmara Municipal de São Paulo
sources.claim_summary: São Paulo Municipal Council: official page of the Parliamentary Inquiry Commission (CPI) on Violence Against Trans and Travesti People — its remit, members, hearings and final report on lethal violence against trans people in the municipality.

Government of Canada travel advice for Brazil (updated Aug 2026): 'Exercise a high degree of caution' with regional advisories; covers safety, entry/exit, health, laws and culture. General travel advice, not trans-specific.

sources.title: LGBTQIA+ travel in Brazil | Intrepid Travel EN
sources.claim_summary: Intrepid Travel country guide: calls Brazil 'progressive' on LGBTQIA+ rights — marriage equality, same-sex adoption and anti-discrimination laws in employment and housing — while noting an active anti-LGBTQIA+ minority and one of the world's highest murder rates of LGBTQIA+ people.

Brazzil magazine (March 2000): historian James N. Green on 'Pleasures in the Parks of Rio de Janeiro during the Brazilian Belle Époque, 1898-1914' - historical account of male same-sex cruising and sexual culture in Rio, documenting the long history of homosexuality in Brazil.
